The edit stales docs/documentation.html and the clarity receipt for SERVICE-SPEC.md, which is the only source of the verify exit 1.

Membership no longer reads payload run_id; F2 and the unit test show a run_id naming S on an unreported address is not enrolled. What remains: (a) the vouching REPORTED entry is any EVENT on S with event == REPORTED, by any actor; the service does not tie it to the run's ATTEMPTED actor, so F3 enrols a forged address by first forging a report on S, which is the same class of exposure HEAD had (anyone who can append on S shapes S's projection); (b) vouching is by address, so every entry on a vouched address is included, including entries by other actors or other runs on the same file (F1), and the first-pass guarantee 'entries on the output address without this run_id are not included' no longer holds by design. Neither (a) nor (b) has a fixture.

repairs.verdict: settled as a reversible default by the evidence; one question remains
repairs.basis: The controller's default, membership from the run's own REPORTED.output_record_addresses, is the linkage the Observation service already uses (record.py reported_addresses) and is now declared in the Record service's own spec; the record-local, revertible change is the lowest tier that can settle it (decisions/0033 Ruling 1). What the evidence does not settle, recorded as J2: whether a projection 'for one subject' should carry every entry on a vouched address or only entries the vouching run's actor produced, and whether the vouching REPORTED must come from the run's own actor. The defeater for the default is a real journal where two runs write the same file and a Finding cites the other run's output as this run's.

second_pass.enrolment_answer: An appender cannot enrol an entry into S's projection without S having reported the address (F2 refused). But 'S having reported' means any actor appended a REPORTED-shaped EVENT on S's subject (F3 succeeded), and once an address is vouched every entry on it by any actor is in (F1). The rule closes the payload-key hole and leaves the subject-append hole that HEAD already had.
